div.l: Withouten̄ eny lenger tarying
At morou when the day began to spⁱringe ·
Vp rose oure host and was oure aldir cok
And gadird us togider in a flocke
And furth we riden̄ a litle more then̄ a pace
Vnto the watring of seint Thomas
And ther͗e oure host began̄ his hors to rest
And seid lordis herkneth if you lest
Ye wote your forward and ye it recorde
If euensong ⁊and morou song both accorde
Lat se now who shal telle the first tale
As eủer mote I drink wine or Ale
Whoso be rebelle to my Iugement
Shal pay for alle that by the wey is spent
Now drawith cutte or that we further twyn̄
He that hath the shortist shalle begynne
¶ Sir knyght coth he my mais̉er ⁊and my lord
Now drawith cutte for that is myn̄ accord
Cometh nere coth he my lady prioresse
And ye sir clerc lat be your shamefastnesse
Ne studieth nat ley hand to euery man̄
Anone to drawe euery wight began̄
And shortly forto telle as it was
Were it by auenture chaunce or cas
The sothe is this the cutte fil to þe knight̄
Of which ful glad and blithe was eủery wight̄
And telle he must his tale as was resoıı̄un
By forewarde and by composicioıı̄un
As ye han herd what nedith wurdis moo .
And when this good man̄ saugh that it was so
As he that wise was and obedient
To hihi kepe his forward by fre assent
He seid syn̄ I . shal begynne the game
What welcum be the cutte in goddis name
Now lat us ride ⁊and herkenth what I sey
And with that wurd we riden̄ furth oure wey
And he began̄ with right a mery chere ·
His tale anone / and seid as ye may here

gentis prelia laurigeno .
